## 0. Agent operating instructions

**What this file is.** The distilled output of the RoomIQ discovery pack (15 screenshots captured in three batches on 2026-11-10: screen inventory, working notes, feature classification, coverage gaps) plus a competitive desk scan (2026-11-13). Sources are listed in `sources/README.md`.

**Authority labels used below.**
- **FACT**: seen in the product. Safe to state, within the limits of what the screen showed.
- **WORKING**: a provisional default the brain operates on until the founder answers. Use it; do not present it as settled strategy to outsiders.
- **OPEN**: undecided. Do not assume an answer. Write `[NEEDS BRAIN]` and keep going.

**How to use it.**
1. Before any customer-facing copy, load the four control files: `rules/writing-rules.md`, `rules/do-not-say.md`, `rules/feature-status.md`, `rules/glossary.md`. They override instinct and older phrasing.

3. Write to one funnel stage (Section 13).
4. Obey the verdicts in Section 9, including the WORKING ones.
5. Run `ops/QA-checklist.md` before returning anything.

**Hard guardrails, never violate:**
1. No accuracy claims about forecasts. RoomIQ has no published backtest. Claim transparency instead.
2. "Underwrite any US address" always travels with the fallback clause in the same sentence.
3. Never name, imply, or describe the data source, and never claim a partnership or affiliation with any platform.
4. No coverage numbers, customer counts, testimonials, or outcome metrics. The customer proof set is empty.
5. UNVERIFIED capabilities are named, never described. ROADMAP items are never mentioned externally.
6. No prices, trials, or limits. `RoomIQ Pro` is the only tier name you may use.

title: RoomIQ Go-To-Market Master Context
heading: 5. What RoomIQ is
text:
## 5. What RoomIQ is

**FACT.** RoomIQ is a web SaaS product for the US rent-by-the-room (coliving) market. It tracks room-level listings: weekly asking rent per room, room move-in fees, occupied and available rooms, listing status, price drops, reviews, and photos. From those it builds market, property, and deal-level views.

**Three modules, one workflow.**

| Stage | Module | What the user gets |
|---|---|---|
| Discover | Dashboard | Choose up to 3 US cities, ZIPs, or a metro group. See Top US markets by Market Score, seasonality (occupancy, fill speed), and an Explore map with hex submarket cells banded Strong, Watch, Weak, Thin, plus property dots by listing status. A property drawer shows KPIs and estimated rental revenue, with hand-offs to the Analyzer and the Predictor. |
| Analyze | Property Analyzer | Search by city, property ID, or listing-title text. Get a Property Signal with a recommendation, a Performance Snapshot, room-segment economics (Private vs Shared bath, Cozy vs Standard size), 7, 30, and 90-day rolling windows, Evidence Quality, Visually Similar Rooms, and Media Studio AI concepts. |
| Underwrite | Property Predictor | Underwrite any US address via geocoded search or a map pin, with fallback support labeled where nearby evidence is thin. See nearby coliving supply within about 3 mi. Fill a baseline profile (type, bedrooms, baths, square feet, bathroom mix, room mix, common areas, garage, transit distance). Run a forecast with automatic model routing and an evidence lookback slider (default 270 days). Get monthly revenue with the formula printed, support level, confidence, illustrative scenarios, comp count, median comp distance, and a best next step. |
| Decide | Deal Calculator (Pro) | Scenario (Conservative, Base, Aggressive), income prefilled from the forecast, purchase, financing. Outputs cash flow, CoC, DSCR, cap rate (outputs not yet captured). |
| Monitor | My Underwrites | Saved property or market reports, re-run to see how the market moved since export (empty state only). |

**The trust design is the product's most distinctive trait (FACT).** The formula is printed under the forecast. "Fallback support" and "Confidence Low" are labeled openly. The median comp distance is disclosed. The scenarios state "not a calibrated prediction interval". Local and expanded comps are shown separately. Soft signals (listing copy, operator behavior) are excluded from forecast inputs on purpose. Revenue estimates carry "Based on observed rents and occupancy, not collected payments." AI concepts carry a burned-in watermark and a disclaimer. The numbers reconcile: segment occupancy rolls up to the property's 62.5%, the best spread is $310 minus $238 = $72, and the forecast formula reproduces to the dollar.

**An AI and computer-vision layer (FACT).** Visually Similar Rooms matches room photos across markets (94 to 96 percent match seen) and shows each match's weekly price and days to fill. Media Studio generates upgrade concepts on listing photos with five presets (Add desk, Add ceiling fan, Repaint neutral, LVP flooring, Stage empty room).

**Platform (FACT).** A `RoomIQ Pro` badge, entitlement chips ("Unlimited analyzer access", "Unlimited baseline runs"), a Pro-only Deal Calculator, light and dark themes, and a Privacy choices link. Maps run on Leaflet with OpenStreetMap and CARTO tiles. A FEMA flood layer toggle exists.

**What RoomIQ is not.** Not a listing marketplace, not a property manager, not a short-term rental tool, not a lender, not a legal or compliance service.

title: RoomIQ Go-To-Market Master Context
heading: 7. Competitive market analysis
text:
## 7. Competitive market analysis

Full analysis: `reference/competitive-analysis.md`. Battlecards: `reference/competitor-battlecards.md`. Every rival fact is from public pages scanned on 2026-11-13 and must be re-verified before external use.

**Market shape (WORKING).** Rent-by-the-room investors today assemble an underwriting picture from five kinds of tools, none built at the room level for an investor evaluating properties they do not yet own:

| Alternative | Examples | What it does well | Where it stops |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spreadsheets and forums | Personal models, investor forums, coaches | Free, flexible, community wisdom | Assumptions typed by hand, no market evidence |
| Platform-native host tools | The marketplaces' own host dashboards and calculators | Real booking data for their own hosts, free to them | One platform's view, built for its hosts, self-reported |
| Short-term rental analytics | AirDNA, Mashvisor, Rabbu | Deep nightly-stay data, investor workflows | Nightly stays, not weekly room rents |
| Whole-unit rent comps | Rentometer, HelloData, RentCast | Address-level rent comps, APIs | Units, not rooms |
| Deal calculators | DealCheck and similar | Cash flow, CoC, DSCR, cap rate | No market evidence for room revenue |

**Scoring vectors (WORKING):** granularity (room vs unit vs night), evidence transparency (shows formula, support, confidence), underwriting depth (address to financed returns in one flow), and visual evidence (photo-based comps).

**The wedge (WORKING).** Room-level evidence plus visible uncertainty. Competitors either work at the wrong unit (night, unit) or ask the investor to type the revenue assumption. RoomIQ starts from observed room rents and says how much to trust the result.

**Primary rival (WORKING):** the status quo, a spreadsheet plus a platform's host calculator. Win by showing the room-level evidence the spreadsheet lacks and the uncertainty the calculator hides.

title: RoomIQ Go-To-Market Master Context
heading: 8. Ideal customer profile
text:
## 8. Ideal customer profile

Full personas and buying committee: `reference/icp-personas.md`.

**Audience A, acquiring investors (WORKING primary).** Individuals and small teams buying or converting single-family homes into rent-by-the-room properties in US Sun Belt metros. Jobs: pick a market, check supply near an address, forecast stabilized revenue, decide the room mix (garage, bathrooms), test financed returns, keep the underwrite. Evidence: the product's end-to-end flow (Dashboard to Predictor to Deal Calculator to My Underwrites), the "Forecast Stabilized Revenue" hand-off, the "investor-grade" and "investors actually underwrite" UI copy.

**Audience B, operating hosts (WORKING secondary).** Operators running one to roughly twenty rent-by-the-room houses who want to price rooms, benchmark properties, and plan upgrades. Evidence: the Analyzer (Property Signal, segments, rolling windows), visual comps, Media Studio, rent guidance, house rules.

**Not a GTM audience yet: lenders, brokers, acquisition analysts.** The product hints at them (DSCR, Evidence Quality) but targeting them needs a published backtest first. Do not write for them until a decision says so.

**Geography (FACT for presets, WORKING for targeting).** The seven preset metros are all Sun Belt: Dallas–Fort Worth, Orlando, Houston, Phoenix, Atlanta, Las Vegas, Jacksonville. Demos and early targeting stay there.

**Buying committee for Audience A:** the investor (decides and pays), a spouse or JV partner (approves capital), a DSCR or portfolio lender (influences, cares about evidence), a coach or mentor community (influences tool choice), the operator or property manager (uses the Analyzer later).

**Design-partner profile (WORKING):** an investor with at least one active rent-by-the-room deal under evaluation in a covered metro, who will run it through the Predictor live and share what they decided.

text:
## 10. Value proposition: acquiring investors

Full pillars and reasons to believe: `reference/value-proposition-investors.md`.

**Promise (WORKING):** Know what each room can earn before you buy the house, and how much to trust the number.

**Pillars:**
1. **Find the market.** Rank US markets by Market Score, see seasonality, and spot strong and thin submarkets on the map (C01, C02, C03, C05).
2. **Underwrite at the room level.** Forecast monthly revenue for any US address from weekly room rents, occupancy, and your room mix, with the formula, support level, and confidence on screen, and fallback support labeled where nearby evidence is thin (C21, C27, C28).

text:
## 12. Positioning statement

**Category (WORKING):** room-level market intelligence and underwriting.
**Niche:** US rent-by-the-room housing.

For US rent-by-the-room investors deciding where to buy, what a house will earn, and how to price its rooms, RoomIQ is room-level market intelligence and underwriting that shows its evidence. Short-term rental analytics model nightly stays and rent comps model whole units; RoomIQ works in the unit this business runs on, the room, priced weekly. And where a spreadsheet hides its guesses, every RoomIQ forecast prints its formula, its comps, and how much to trust it.

**Differentiation and defensibility (WORKING).** Room-level history compounds: each day of observed room rents and fill events deepens the evidence behind every score and forecast. The transparency design is a product posture, not a feature, and is hard to retrofit onto tools built to show a single confident number.

**The two objections that matter most:**
- "Where does your data come from?" Answer from `reference/objection-handling.md` only, without naming a source, until G11 is answered.
- "How accurate is the forecast?" "We do not claim accuracy yet. Every forecast shows its formula, its comps, how far away they are, and a confidence label, so you can judge it yourself."

title: Do not say
heading: Hard bans
text:
## Hard bans

| Do not say | Say instead |
|---|---|
| Accuracy: "accurate forecast", "precise", "predicts revenue", "within X%", "proven model" | "Every forecast shows its formula, its comps, and a confidence label." No backtest exists (G14). |
| Universal coverage: "any market", "every property", "complete coverage", "all US markets" | "Underwrite any US address. Where nearby evidence is thin, RoomIQ labels the forecast fallback support and shows its confidence." |
| Coverage numbers: "properties tracked", "rooms tracked", "thousands of listings" | Nothing until G13 is answered. Screenshot counts (412 in DFW) are one capture, not a claim. |
| Data source: "PadSplit data", "scraped", "official data", "partnered with", "integrated with" | "Built from observed room listings in the markets RoomIQ covers." Never name or imply a source or partner (G11). |
| Real time: "real-time", "live data" | "Metrics show their as-of date." |
| Income language: "income", "earnings", "collected rent", "cash flow guaranteed" | "Estimated rental revenue, based on observed rents and occupancy, not collected payments." |
| Financial advice: "best deals", "guaranteed returns", "will cash flow", "bank-approved", "lender-ready" | "Model cash flow, cash-on-cash, DSCR, and cap rate from the forecast and your own inputs. For information, not financial advice." |
| Legal status: "legal in your city", "compliant", "zoning approved", "local law" | "Compare an operating checklist with recorded local policies. Not legal advice; confirm local rules." |
| AI everywhere: "AI-powered", "AI predicts", "machine learning forecast" | Name the capability. Only visual comps and AI concepts carry AI framing (G19). |
| AI concepts as results: "after photo", "your renovated room", "see the results", "boost rent by" | "Preview an AI concept of an upgrade, watermarked as AI-generated. No validated economics yet." |
| Visual comps as value: "worth the same", "value comps", "equally valuable" | "Rooms that look like this one, with their weekly price and days to fill." |
| Market Score internals: "Market Score measures", "based on demand and supply" | "A 0 to 100 Market Score with a letter grade." (G18) |
| Prices and limits: "pricing starts at", "plan costs", "free trial", "unlimited plan", "money-back" | Nothing. Pricing is undecided (G07). `RoomIQ Pro` may be named as shown. |
| Invented proof: testimonials, customer counts, "investors trust", "users earn" | The closed proof set in `ops/copy-bank.md`. Customer proof today: none. Write `[PROOF POINT NEEDED]`. |
| Unverified features described: what amenity ROI, house rules, rent guidance, layouts, cohorts, or forecasts return | Name them as present in the product. Describe output only after status moves to SHIPPED. |
| Flood: "flood risk score", "insurance determination" | "Check the FEMA flood hazard layer on the map. Not an insurance or regulatory determination." |
| Category confusion: "Airbnb", "short-term rental", "vacation rental" | "rent-by-the-room", "weekly room rents". |

heading: Metrics and outputs
text:
## Metrics and outputs

| Term | Rule |
|---|---|
| Market Score | A 0 to 100 score with a letter grade. Never describe its inputs (confirm). |
| Occupancy | Occupied rooms divided by total rooms. Room-level, never unit-level. |
| Avg weekly asking | Mean asking rent per room per week. Rents are weekly in this category. |
| Fill speed, days to fill | How fast a vacant room is re-leased (confirm formula). |
| Occupancy Health | Submarket cell signal from observed occupied rooms. |
| Strong, Watch, Weak, Thin | Occupancy Score bands. "Thin" means too little evidence, never "low demand". |

| Property Signal | The action label on a property (seen: `Useful benchmark`) plus its recommendation. |
| Best spread | Largest average weekly price gap between room segments. |
| Room segment | Rooms grouped by bathroom (Private, Shared) or size (Cozy, Standard). |

## The distinction that must never blur

**Estimated** versus **actual**. Every RoomIQ number is an estimate built from observed listings, and it travels with its evidence: the as-of date, the support level, the confidence label. A forecast is never "accurate", an estimate is never "income", and an AI concept is never the property.

These apply to every word of RoomIQ output: web, decks, scripts, release notes, in-app copy, and AI-generated text inside the product.

title: Writing rules
heading: Mechanics
text:
## Mechanics
- No em dashes anywhere. Use commas, colons, or two sentences. En dashes stay only inside official metro names ("Dallas–Fort Worth").
- Banned words: leverage, unlock, seamless, robust, streamline, cutting-edge, empower, elevate, revolutionize, game-changing, best-in-class, world-class, supercharge, turbocharge, harness, delve, tapestry, testament, foster, facilitate, utilize, myriad, plethora, pivotal, crucial, vital, skyrocket, effortless, unparalleled, groundbreaking.
- "Leverage" is banned in its finance sense too. Say financing, debt, or loan-to-value.
- Avoid in their figurative sense: landscape, navigate, journey, realm.
- Paragraphs of one to three sentences. Front-load the point.
- Numbers over adjectives. Every number carries its unit and window: "$260 avg weekly asking, last 90 days", never "$260".
- Rents are weekly per room. Revenue is monthly per property. Say which.
- Use the product's own labels, spelled as the UI spells them (`rules/glossary.md`).

title: Writing rules
heading: Tone
text:
## Tone
Plain, numerate, and candid, like a good underwriting memo. The readers put their own money and debt behind a decision, so they trust evidence and distrust hype. When the evidence is thin, say so before they find out: RoomIQ's own UI does this ("Fallback support", "Confidence Low"), and the copy matches it.

Right register: an analyst explaining a comp set. Wrong register: "passive income" real estate marketing, urgency tricks, and lifestyle promises.

title: Writing rules
heading: Writing for the ear (demos, video, webinars)
text:
## Writing for the ear (demos, video, webinars)
- Short spoken sentences. One clause where you would write two.
- Second person, one listener, contractions.
- Say what is on screen before you interpret it: "This tile shows 87.5 percent occupancy."
- Say confidence labels out loud. Never skip "fallback" or "low confidence" for pacing.
- Read it aloud before it ships. Cut what you stumble on.

# Competitive market analysis

Load for: competitive questions, comparison pages, "how is this different from X". Distills: S7 desk scan of public pages, 2026-11-13. Every rival fact below is from the rival's or a third party's public page on that date. Re-verify before any external use, and record the re-check date here.

title: Competitive market analysis
heading: Market shape
text:
## Market shape
There is no established category of room-level investor analytics. Rent-by-the-room investors assemble a view from five alternatives plus the status quo.

| Alternative | Representative tools | Built for | Unit of analysis | Where it stops for this buyer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Status quo | Spreadsheets, forums, coaches | Anyone | Whatever the investor types | No market evidence behind the room rent assumption |
| Platform-native host tools | Marketplace host dashboards, earnings calculators, market reports | That platform's own hosts | Room, inside one platform | One platform's view; self-reported; built for hosts already on it |
| Short-term rental analytics | AirDNA, Mashvisor, Rabbu | Airbnb-style hosts and investors | Night | Nightly stays, not weekly room rents |
| Whole-unit rent comps | Rentometer, HelloData, RentCast | Landlords, multifamily, brokers | Unit | Whole units, not rooms |
| Deal calculators | DealCheck and similar | Buy-and-hold investors | Deal | Revenue is an assumption the user types |
| Data vendors and research | SFR Analytics (room-for-rent analysis), operator reports | Analysts | Varies | Research and data feeds, not an underwriting workflow |

title: Competitive market analysis
heading: Scoring vectors (WORKING)
text:
## Scoring vectors (WORKING)
1. **Granularity.** Room, unit, or night.
2. **Evidence transparency.** Does the output show its formula, support, and confidence?
3. **Underwriting depth.** Address to forecast to financed returns in one flow.
4. **Visual evidence.** Photo-based comps.
5. **Coverage independence.** Breadth across sources and markets. OPEN for RoomIQ (G11, G13), so never claimed.

title: Competitive market analysis
heading: Where RoomIQ sits (WORKING, unscored)
text:
## Where RoomIQ sits (WORKING, unscored)
- Strong on vectors 1 to 4 as SHIPPED capabilities.
- Unknown on vector 5. Do not compete on it.
- Weak where rivals have depth RoomIQ cannot claim: years of history (AirDNA), API ecosystems (Rentometer, HelloData), and the platforms' first-party booking data.

title: Competitive market analysis
heading: The wedge
text:
## The wedge
Room-level evidence plus visible uncertainty. Rivals either work at the wrong unit or leave the revenue assumption to the investor. RoomIQ starts from observed room rents and says how far to trust the result.

title: Competitive market analysis
heading: Public facts gathered (2026-11-13, re-verify before use)
text:
## Public facts gathered (2026-11-13, re-verify before use)
- A leading marketplace's host tools show each room's price against the metro average and a market insights map; the marketplace publishes monthly market reports and an earnings calculator. Its occupancy data is self-reported from its own bookings.
- AirDNA is a short-term rental data platform, widely cited as the default for STR market research.
- Mashvisor is positioned on comparing short-term and long-term rental strategies on one property.
- Rabbu offers short-term rental tools free and runs a property marketplace.
- Rentometer offers address-level rent estimates and an API built on whole-unit inputs (bedrooms, bathrooms, building type).
- HelloData offers multifamily rent comps and a rent comps API, including concession tracking.
- DealCheck analyzes buy-and-hold, rehab, Airbnb, and vacation rentals; coliving is not listed as a property type.
- SFR Analytics published an analysis of room-for-rent listings against whole-home rent estimates; it is research, not a room-level product.

heading: Competitor battlecards
text:
# Competitor battlecards

Load for: sales calls, objection prep, comparison copy. Distills: `reference/competitive-analysis.md`. Three lines per rival: their real strength first, their real gap, how RoomIQ wins. Rival facts dated 2026-11-13; re-verify before external use.

Rule: lead with the rival's genuine strength. A card that pretends a rival is weak loses the room the moment the prospect knows better.

title: Competitor battlecards
heading: The status quo: spreadsheet plus forums
text:
## The status quo: spreadsheet plus forums
- **Strength.** Free, fully flexible, and the investor trusts their own assumptions.
- **Gap.** The room rent and occupancy inputs are guesses; nothing shows how sure the investor should be.
- **How RoomIQ wins.** Run their address live. Show the forecast with the formula, the comps, and the confidence label, then let them compare it to the number in their sheet.

title: Competitor battlecards
heading: Platform-native host tools (a marketplace's own dashboard and calculator)
text:
## Platform-native host tools (a marketplace's own dashboard and calculator)
- **Strength.** First-party booking data for that platform's rooms, free to its hosts, and integrated with how they already operate.
- **Gap.** One platform's view, built for hosts already on it, self-reported. An investor evaluating a house they do not own yet is not the primary user.
- **How RoomIQ wins.** Underwrite any US address before the purchase, with room-level evidence and fallback support labeled where nearby evidence is thin. Never claim independence from any platform or name a data source (D-04).

title: Competitor battlecards
heading: AirDNA
text:
## AirDNA
- **Strength.** Deep short-term rental data and wide recognition as the STR research default.
- **Gap.** Built for nightly stays. Weekly room rents, room occupancy, and fill speed are not its model.
- **How RoomIQ wins.** "AirDNA is built for nightly stays. RoomIQ models weekly room rents and room occupancy." Never "better than AirDNA".

title: Competitor battlecards
heading: Mashvisor
text:
## Mashvisor
- **Strength.** Compares short-term and long-term strategies on the same property, investor-oriented workflow.
- **Gap.** Rent-by-the-room is not one of the strategies it is known for.
- **How RoomIQ wins.** For an investor already set on rent-by-the-room, RoomIQ works at the room level from the first screen.

title: Competitor battlecards
heading: Rabbu
text:
## Rabbu
- **Strength.** Free short-term rental tools.
- **Gap.** Short-term rental focus.
- **How RoomIQ wins.** Different unit, different decision. Do not compete on price (pricing OPEN).

title: Competitor battlecards
heading: Rentometer, HelloData, RentCast
text:
## Rentometer, HelloData, RentCast
- **Strength.** Address-level rent comps and mature APIs; HelloData tracks concessions in multifamily.
- **Gap.** Whole units. A rent-by-the-room house earns from rooms with different bath and size mixes.
- **How RoomIQ wins.** Room segments and best spread: show that a private-bath room and a shared-bath room in the same house earn differently ($310 vs $238 per week in screen 07).

title: Competitor battlecards
heading: DealCheck and similar calculators
text:
## DealCheck and similar calculators
- **Strength.** Mature deal math: cash flow, CoC, DSCR, cap rate, multiple strategies.
- **Gap.** Revenue is typed by the user; coliving is not a listed property type.
- **How RoomIQ wins.** The Deal Calculator starts from the RoomIQ forecast instead of a guess (C31, PARTIAL: show inputs prefilled, do not show outputs until captured).

title: Competitor battlecards
heading: What to never say about any rival
text:
## What to never say about any rival
Rumors, pricing you have not verified this month, "they scrape", "their data is wrong", or any claim about a rival's roadmap.

text:
## Thesis
Rent-by-the-room investors learn from each other in public: forums, groups, podcasts, YouTube. They distrust tool marketing and trust worked examples. So RoomIQ content teaches the underwriting method first, shows the product second, and never asks for trust it has not earned with arithmetic.

text:
## How the channels feed each other
1. Community answers surface the questions people actually ask (signal type LANGUAGE).
2. Repeated questions become articles and short videos (Campaign 2).
3. Articles carry one call to action into a demo or a trial (stage 3 to 4).
4. Demos produce objections and proof requests, which return to the signal log and sharpen the next piece.

title: Content engine, education-led content
heading: Archetypes to rotate
text:
## Archetypes to rotate
- **The worked example.** One house, one question, the numbers shown. Covered metro only.
- **The method piece.** How to think about one underwriting variable (room mix, shared-bath pressure, fill speed).
- **The myth check.** A common rule of thumb, tested against what the evidence shows. Only with numbers RoomIQ can show on screen.
- **The honest limitation.** What RoomIQ does when evidence is thin, and why the label matters.
- **The operator teardown.** Room segments of a property explained (blurred host and photos).

**Edit.** Cut the warm-up. Run `python3 tools/brain.py lint`. Check every capability against `rules/feature-status.md`. Read the opening aloud.

title: Demo playbook, founder-led demos
heading: The demo path (covered metro, about 20 minutes)
text:
## The demo path (covered metro, about 20 minutes)
1. **Dashboard.** Choose a Sun Belt metro preset. Show Top US markets by Market Score and the Explore map bands. Say what "Thin" means: too little evidence, not weak demand.
2. **Drawer.** Open a property. Read the revenue disclaimer aloud: "Based on observed rents and occupancy, not collected payments."
3. **Analyzer.** Property Signal, room segments, best spread, rolling windows. Do the arithmetic out loud: segment occupancy reconciles to the property.
4. **Visual comps.** Scroll past any non-bedroom photo without comment; never make one a talking point (D-Q18).
5. **Predictor.** Use an address in Dallas, Austin, Houston, Atlanta, Phoenix, or Tampa that you have tested that day. Show nearby supply, complete the room mix fully (avoids D-Q26), run the forecast, read the formula, the support level, and the confidence label aloud.
6. **Deal Calculator.** Type every input yourself, including the interest rate. Never show defaults (D-Q30, D-Q31). Say "for information, not financial advice".
7. **Close.** Offer to run the prospect's own address, if it is in a covered metro.

title: ICP and personas
heading: Audience A, acquiring investors (primary)
text:
## Audience A, acquiring investors (primary)

**Who.** Individual investors and small teams (one to five people) buying or converting single-family homes and townhouses into rent-by-the-room properties, in US Sun Belt metros first.

**Trigger moments.** A house under contract or in diligence. Entering a new metro. Deciding whether to convert a garage. A lender asking for a revenue basis on a DSCR loan.

**Jobs to be done.**
1. Pick a market worth buying in.
2. Check how much coliving supply already sits near an address.
3. Estimate stabilized monthly revenue room by room.
4. Decide the room mix: bathrooms, garage, common space.
5. See whether the deal still works with financing.
6. Keep the underwrite and re-check it later.

**What they use today.** A spreadsheet with typed-in room rents, a marketplace's host calculator, forum threads, a coach's rule of thumb.

**What wins them.** Seeing room-level evidence for their own address, with the uncertainty labeled. The math reproducing on screen.

**What blocks them.** "Where does the data come from?" "How accurate is it?" A first run on an uncovered address that returns a fallback forecast with Low confidence.

title: ICP and personas
heading: Audience B, operating hosts (secondary)
text:
## Audience B, operating hosts (secondary)

**Who.** Operators running roughly one to twenty rent-by-the-room houses, often self-managed, who price rooms weekly and fight vacancy.

**Trigger moments.** A room sits empty past its usual fill time. Planning a refresh. Setting the price for a newly added room. Comparing two of their own houses.

**Jobs to be done.**
1. See which rooms earn a premium and why (bath, size).
2. Price a room from rooms that look like it.
3. Watch direction over 7, 30, and 90 days.
4. Decide which upgrade is worth doing.

**What wins them.** A best spread or a visual comp that changes a price this week.

**What blocks them.** Not seeing their own property tracked. Distrust of AI images. Price sensitivity (OPEN, G07).

title: Innovation accounting, the protocol
heading: Innovation accounting, the protocol
text:
# Innovation accounting, the protocol

Load for: planning any experiment, reviewing results, deciding pivot or persevere, and the weekly triage. The files it governs live in `innovation/` and `ops/`. Status: DECIDED operating model (D-12).

title: Innovation accounting, the protocol
heading: Why RoomIQ needs it
text:
## Why RoomIQ needs it
RoomIQ is a shipped product with no customer proof, no measured funnel, and several leap-of-faith assumptions (data rights, coverage depth, willingness to pay). In that state, activity is easy to confuse with progress. Innovation accounting forces every activity to answer one question: what did we learn, and does it move a decision?

title: Innovation accounting, the protocol
heading: The three steps, mapped to files
text:
## The three steps, mapped to files
1. **Establish the baseline.** Measure where the funnel actually is today. `innovation/metrics.md` holds the metric tree; every baseline starts as "not measured" and is filled only from real data.
2. **Tune the engine.** Run experiments that each target one assumption and one metric, with the success threshold written before the result exists. `innovation/experiments.md`.
3. **Pivot or persevere.** On a fixed cadence, compare results to thresholds and decide. Decisions go to `ops/decisions.md` with the evidence that moved them.

title: Innovation accounting, the protocol
heading: The data flow (the snowball)
text:
## The data flow (the snowball)
```
ACTIVITY (what we did)        -> ops/activity-log.md
   produces
SIGNAL (what we heard/saw)    -> ops/signal-log.md      triage: NOISE | WATCH | PATCH | AMEND
   moves
ASSUMPTION (what we believe)  -> innovation/assumptions.md  UNTESTED | TESTING | VALIDATED | INVALIDATED
   tested by
EXPERIMENT (pre-registered)   -> innovation/experiments.md  PLANNED | RUNNING | DONE
   produces
LEARNING + DECISION           -> ops/decisions.md       PERSEVERE | PIVOT | ITERATE | KILL
   amends
LEDGERS -> COPY -> ASSETS     -> rules/, ops/copy-bank.md, pages/
   which create the next ACTIVITY
```
Every arrow is a file edit, so git history is the audit trail. `python3 tools/brain.py metrics` rolls the counts up.

title: Innovation accounting, the protocol
heading: Rules that keep it honest
text:
## Rules that keep it honest
- **Thresholds before results.** An experiment with no pre-set threshold is an anecdote. Write metric, threshold, sample size, and end date when it is PLANNED.
- **Actionable metrics only.** A metric must be per cohort, per audience, and tied to a decision. Totals (signups, page views, generations) are vanity unless divided by something that matters.
- **One assumption per experiment.** If a result could be explained by two assumptions, split the experiment.
- **Learning counts even when the result is bad.** An INVALIDATED assumption is progress; log it with the same care.
- **No result inflates a claim.** A validated assumption changes a ledger only through the AMEND procedure, and only proof that is permissioned enters `ops/copy-bank.md`.

title: Innovation accounting, the protocol
heading: Cadence
text:
## Cadence
- Weekly: triage signals, update experiment status, increment WATCH counters.
- Monthly: snapshot (`snapshots/`), compare each metric to its baseline, review assumptions.
- Every 90 days or at a learning milestone: pivot or persevere meeting, logged as a decision.

title: Innovation accounting, the protocol
heading: Learning milestones (WORKING)
text:
## Learning milestones (WORKING)
1. Ten design-partner sessions logged with verbatims (EXP-001).
2. Activation defined from evidence and measured on a first cohort.
3. Data rights and coverage confirmed (R1, R2).
4. A backtest published or explicitly deferred (R3).
5. First paid conversions at the Deal Calculator gate (A3).

title: Innovation accounting, the protocol
heading: Brain health metrics (learning velocity)
text:
## Brain health metrics (learning velocity)
Signals logged per week, WATCH items promoted, AMENDs per month, median days from signal to decision, experiments completed per month, assumptions resolved, ledger staleness. These measure whether the brain is compounding. `tools/brain.py metrics` reports them.

text:
# Metrics methodology, how each number is built

Load for: support answers, methodology pages, demo explanations, in-app help text, and grounding an in-product assistant. Distills: S2 glossary section 4 and consistency checks section 8. Each row says how far the definition is verified. "Verified" means the arithmetic reproduces from a screenshot; "working" means a reasonable reading pending founder confirmation (G18 and related).

| Metric | Definition | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Occupancy | Occupied rooms divided by total rooms | Verified | 5/8 = 62.5%, 7/8 = 87.5% |
| Avg daily price | Weekly price divided by 7 | Verified | $260 / 7 = $37 |
| Best spread | Largest average weekly price gap between segments | Verified | $310 minus $238 = $72 |
| Segment 90-day occupancy | Room-weighted, rolls up to the property | Verified | (3 x 71.5 + 5 x 57.1) / 8 = 62.5% |
| Forecast monthly revenue | Price x rooms x occupancy x 4.35 weeks | Verified | $282 x 1.0 x 89.5% x 4.35 = $1,098 |
| Illustrative scenarios | Forecast minus and plus 10 percent | Verified | $988 and $1,207 |
| Visual comp medians | Median price and median days to fill of the matches | Verified | $245, 9.5 days |
| Estimated rental revenue | About avg weekly asking x occupied rooms x weeks in window | Working | Reproduces within 1% on screen 06; not on screen 04 |
| Occ delta, price delta | Change against the prior equal-length window, likely relative percent | Working | 51.4% on the 30-day window |
| Volatility | Dispersion within the window, unit unknown | Working | 4.37, 11.15, 22.82 |
| Market Score | 0 to 100 composite with a letter grade | Working | Inputs unknown (G18) |
| Occupancy Health | Cell demand signal from observed occupied rooms | Working | UI helper text |
| Evidence-adjusted | Scores shrunk for small samples | Working | Legend footer |
| Fill speed, days to fill | Time for a vacant room to re-lease | Working | Chip colors: about 5 days or less green, 33 or more yellow |
| Completeness, history coverage | Share of expected fields present; share of the window observed | Working | 100% and 100% seen |
| Confidence | Forecast label, Low seen | Working | Levels unknown |

## Two weekly-to-monthly factors, documented so numbers reconcile
The Predictor uses 4.35 weeks per month (52.2 / 12). The Analyzer's 30-day windows imply 30 / 7 = 4.29. Expect small differences between modules for the same rent.

title: Objection handling
heading: "Where does your data come from?"
text:
## "Where does your data come from?"
Honest answer today: "RoomIQ is built from observed room listings in the markets it covers, tracked over time at the room level. Every metric shows its as-of date, and every property shows an Evidence Quality score so you can see how complete the history is."
Never name or imply a source, a partner, or a collection method (D-04). If pushed: "I'll get you a written answer on sourcing" and log the signal as OBJECTION.

title: Objection handling
heading: "How accurate is the forecast?"
text:
## "How accurate is the forecast?"
"We don't claim accuracy yet. What you get instead is the forecast's working: the formula, the number of comps, how far away they are, whether local evidence was enough, and a confidence label. On a thin-evidence address it will tell you that, in red."
If the founder publishes a backtest (G14), this answer changes by AMEND.

title: Objection handling
heading: "Does it cover my market?"
text:
## "Does it cover my market?"
"Run your address and RoomIQ shows nearby coliving supply within about three miles first. If evidence is thin, the forecast says fallback support and shows its confidence." In a live call, choose the address yourself only in covered metros (D-06).

title: Objection handling
heading: "My house isn't on any platform yet. Does that matter?"
text:
## "My house isn't on any platform yet. Does that matter?"
"No. The Property Predictor underwrites any US address from your baseline profile: type, bedrooms, bathrooms, room mix, and if nearby evidence is thin the forecast says fallback support. Tracked properties use their own history; new ones use the bounded underwriting path."

title: Objection handling
heading: "Why not just use AirDNA?"
text:
## "Why not just use AirDNA?"
"AirDNA is built for nightly stays. A rent-by-the-room house earns weekly, room by room, and its rooms earn differently by bathroom and size. RoomIQ models that unit."

title: Objection handling
heading: "I already have a spreadsheet."
text:
## "I already have a spreadsheet."
"Keep it. Put RoomIQ's forecast next to your room rent assumption and see where they differ, with the comps behind the difference."

title: Objection handling
heading: "Are the AI images real?"
text:
## "Are the AI images real?"
"No, and the product says so on every one: AI-generated, not actual property condition, watermarked into the downloaded file. They are concepts for planning, with no validated rent impact yet."

title: Objection handling
heading: "Can I give this to my lender?"
text:
## "Can I give this to my lender?"
"You can share the underwrite as your own analysis. RoomIQ isn't a lender product or an appraisal, and the Deal Calculator is for information, not financial advice." Do not say "lender-ready".

title: Objection handling
heading: "What does it cost?"
text:
## "What does it cost?"
Pricing is not decided (D-11). Say: "I'll send current plans after the call." Never quote a number.

title: Objection handling
heading: "Is rent-by-the-room legal where I'm buying?"
text:
## "Is rent-by-the-room legal where I'm buying?"
"RoomIQ compares an operating checklist with recorded local policies, but it isn't legal advice. Check local occupancy and rooming-house rules with someone qualified." House rules output is UNVERIFIED (C24): do not describe it.

title: Objection handling
heading: "What does Market Score measure?"

"It's a 0 to 100 score with a letter grade that ranks markets for this model." Do not list inputs until G18 is answered.

heading: How to update a row
text:
## How to update a row
1. A signal or experiment result arrives. Add the evidence in a short phrase with its date and source ID (signal date, EXP id).
2. Change status only when an experiment's pre-set threshold is met or missed, or a single verified fact settles a RISK row.

4. Re-rank riskiness monthly in the snapshot. Work on the highest riskiness first.

Every GTM activity is logged in `ops/activity-log.md`, every market input in `ops/signal-log.md`, and every experiment states its metric and success threshold before it runs (`innovation/experiments.md`).

Rationale: RoomIQ is pre-proof. Without a baseline and pre-registered thresholds, early activity produces vanity numbers and no learning. The brain already holds the ledgers, so adding the accounting costs one file per concept.

**What this does not change:** the claim ledger, the status ledger, or any channel rule.
**Downstream:** `innovation/` files seeded 2026-11-13. Owner: founder.

## 2026-11-13 D-10 Channel mix (WORKING)
In: founder-led demos and sales calls, education content, community participation, product-led trial, product and release copy. Not yet: paid ads and cold outreach at volume.

Rationale: pre-baseline, paid spend buys traffic without a measured activation rate to judge it against, and cold outreach at volume carries brand risk while the data-source question is open. Founder-led conversations produce the signals the ledgers need fastest.
**Trigger to flip:** founder answer to G01, or a snapshot showing an activation baseline exists.
**What this does not change:** warm follow-ups to people who asked for information are in scope.

text:
## 2026-11-13 D-09 Lead message is visible evidence, not accuracy (WORKING)
RoomIQ leads with "every number shows its evidence": formula, support level, comp distance, confidence.

Rationale: accuracy cannot be claimed (D-05), while the transparency design is SHIPPED and visible on screen 14. For buyers who put debt behind a decision, a number that admits its uncertainty is more credible than a confident one.
**Trigger to revisit:** a published backtest (G14), which would allow adding a scoped accuracy claim beside transparency.
**What this does not change:** the fallback clause stays mandatory on "any US address".

## 2026-11-13 D-08 Category framing (WORKING)
Room-level market intelligence and underwriting for US rent-by-the-room housing.

Rationale: "coliving analytics" is narrower than the product's underwriting depth; "real estate analytics" invites comparison with whole-unit and short-term rental tools on their own terms.
**Trigger to revisit:** founder answer to G05, or three independent prospects describing the category in other words (signal log).
**What this does not change:** glossary terms.

## 2026-11-13 D-07 Audience order (WORKING)
Acquiring investors first, operating hosts second, never blended in one asset. Lenders, brokers, and analysts are not a GTM audience yet.

Rationale: the product's full flow (Dashboard to Predictor to Deal Calculator to My Underwrites) and its UI copy ("investor-grade", "Property facts that investors actually underwrite") point at acquisition decisions. The Analyzer and Media Studio serve operators.
**Trigger to revisit:** founder answer to G05, or the design-partner program (EXP-001) showing operators activate faster.
**What this does not change:** operators keep their own value proposition and funnel.

Demos run only in well-covered metros (Dallas, Austin, Houston, Atlanta, Phoenix, Tampa) and never cross a known defect (D-Q26, D-Q28, D-Q30, D-Q18).

Rationale: the NYC capture produced a $282 per week room price on comps a median 82.88 mi away. A prospect's first run is the moment of highest drop-off risk.

text:
## Rituals

| Ritual | Frequency | Owner | Work |
|---|---|---|---|
| Signal triage | Weekly, Monday | Founder | Disposition every new signal, increment WATCH counters, execute PATCHes, update experiment status |
| Activity review | Weekly, Monday | Founder | Fill outcomes for last week's activities; link each to its experiment |

title: Signal log
heading: Signal log
text:
# Signal log

Raw market input, captured before judgment. Every signal from a prospect, customer, competitor, channel, or the product itself lands here first. Newest at the top. Append with `python3 tools/brain.py log-signal` or by hand in the format below.

**Keep the verbatim.** The words a real buyer used, before we taught them ours, are the most valuable thing a signal carries.

title: Signal log
heading: How to use this file
text:
## How to use this file

**Types:** OBJECTION, LANGUAGE, PROOF, STATUS, COMPETITIVE, SEGMENT, CHANNEL, LOSS, RISK.

**Dispositions:**
- `UNTRIAGED`: captured by a tool or a person, awaiting the weekly triage. Never left past one triage cycle.
- `NOISE`: one instance, no pattern. Logged and closed.
- `WATCH (n/N)`: plausible pattern awaiting corroboration. Increment as instances arrive.
- `PATCH`: changes copy, not strategy. Route, edit, done.
- `AMEND`: changes a ledger, a position, or a rule. Full amendment procedure plus a `ops/decisions.md` entry.

**Corroboration thresholds** (proposed 2026-11-13, confirm with G10):

| Signal class | Threshold to act |
|---|---|
| Opinion, preference, language, objection | 3 independent instances within 60 days |
| Verifiable fact: status, proof, competitive, risk | 1 verified instance, act immediately |
| Loss reason | 2 instances, or 1 if the deal was a design partner |
| Channel performance | A full measurement cycle, never a single week |

Default disposition is NOISE. Triage runs weekly (`ops/review-cadence.md`). A WATCH item with no increment in two cycles expires to NOISE, and the expiry is written here.

# Example, community answer for operators

Status: draft gold standard, checked against ledgers 2026-11-13, founder approval pending.
Audience: B, operating hosts. Template: `templates/community-answer.md`.
The question, as asked: "Two rooms in my house keep sitting empty for weeks while the others fill fast. Same price. What am I missing?"

---

Same price is probably the problem. Rooms in one house rarely earn the same, and residents compare them the way you would.

Start with the bathroom. A room with a private bath competes in a different market from a room that shares one. If three rooms share a single bath, those three are fighting each other and every private-bath room nearby. Look at the rooms that fill fast: do they have the bath, the bigger footprint, the window?

Then check fill time, not just occupancy. A room that sits 30 days and then rents at full price may be costing you more than one that rents in 3 days at $15 less a week. Over a quarter, the empty weeks usually win that argument.

What I'd do: list each room with its bath type, size, and how many days it sat last time. Price the slow ones against similar rooms nearby, not against the rest of your house.

Disclosure: I'm building RoomIQ, which breaks properties into room segments by bath and size and shows rooms that look like yours with their weekly price and days to fill. Happy to look at your two rooms with you if useful.

---

title: Adapters, one brain and many doors
heading: Adapters, one brain and many doors
text:
# Adapters, one brain and many doors

The brain is Markdown. Every AI tool differs only in where it looks for standing instructions and what makes it read them. This folder holds the doors. None of them carries strategy, a claim, or a status, except `portable-control-layer.md`, which exists because a chat window cannot follow a pointer.

**One copy of the truth, many doors into it.** Pointer files are generated from one template, `tools/templates/pointer-body.md.tmpl`, by `python3 tools/brain.py adapters --write`. CI fails when any of them drifts (`adapters --check`). Edit the template or the brain, never a generated pointer.

title: Adapters, one brain and many doors
heading: Four ways in, by tool capability
text:
## Four ways in, by tool capability

| Tier | How it loads | Cost per session | Tools |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Native skill or plugin | Indexed, loaded on match | Near zero until triggered | Claude Code (`.claude/skills/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/commands/`) |
| 2. Project instruction file | Always in context or loaded on description match, then opens files | 300 to 600 tokens | Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, Gemini CLI, Cline, Roo, Continue, Kiro, Junie, Amazon Q, Aider, Zed, opencode, Jules, Warp |
| 3. Tool call (MCP) | Agent calls `brain_*` tools on demand | A few hundred tokens plus tool results | Any MCP client |
| 4. Paste or upload | Bundle in the context window | 6,000 to 40,000 tokens per call | ChatGPT, Claude.ai Projects, Gemini Gems, Grok, custom GPTs, raw API calls |

title: Adapters, one brain and many doors
heading: Tier 2, wiring the product codebase (where the copy actually ships)
text:
## Tier 2, wiring the product codebase (where the copy actually ships)

The highest-value door is the RoomIQ application repository: that is where UI strings, release notes, onboarding emails, pricing pages, and in-product LLM prompts get written by Copilot, Cursor, or Codex. Add the brain as a submodule and install the consuming-repo adapters:

```bash
cd ../roomiq-app
git submodule add https://github.com/Saasrelaunchdev/RoomIQGTMBrain gtm-brain
python3 gtm-brain/tools/brain.py adapters --install . --brain-path gtm-brain
```

Shared files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.junie/guidelines.md`) receive a marked block appended at the end; existing content is untouched. MCP configs are deep-merged. `.aider.conf.yml` is written only if absent. A ready-rendered copy for `gtm-brain/` lives in `adapters/consuming-repo/` for review or manual copying. In consuming repos, Cursor and Windsurf rules load on description match, not always.

Use a different `--brain-path` if the brain is checked out elsewhere (for example `../RoomIQGTMBrain`).

title: Adapters, one brain and many doors
heading: Tier 3, MCP
text:
## Tier 3, MCP

`tools/mcp_server.py` exposes the brain as tools, resources, and prompts over stdio. Configs for every client: `adapters/mcp/README.md`. In this repository, `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json`, and `.gemini/settings.json` already register it.

title: Adapters, one brain and many doors
heading: Tier 4, chat models without file access
text:
## Tier 4, chat models without file access

| Surface | What to give it | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Custom GPT, Gemini Gem, Grok custom instructions, small instruction boxes | `adapters/portable-control-layer.md` (about 7,500 characters) | Instructions field |
| Claude.ai Project, ChatGPT Project, Gemini with files | `dist/roomiq-gtm-brain.bundle.md` | Project knowledge or attachment |
| Long-context models, NotebookLM-style tools | `dist/llms-full.txt` | Upload |
| Raw API calls | Portable layer or bundle as the system prompt | `system` or developer message |
| Your own RAG pipeline | `dist/brain.chunks.jsonl`, but inject the control layer directly | Vector store plus system prompt |

For custom GPTs: paste the portable control layer into Instructions, upload `dist/roomiq-gtm-brain.bundle.md` and the four `rules/` files as Knowledge, and add the line "Before answering, search your knowledge for the rules files." Regenerate and re-upload whenever a ledger changes.

**Never retrieve the control layer.** A retrieval miss on the claim ledger is the exact failure this brain exists to prevent. Inject `rules/` directly; retrieve only reference and execution files.

title: Adapters, one brain and many doors
heading: The conformance check, run in each tool after wiring
text:
## The conformance check, run in each tool after wiring

Open a fresh session and ask:

| # | Prompt | Pass |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | "What audiences does RoomIQ sell to?" | Names investors and operators, never blended |
| 2 | "Write a tweet saying RoomIQ's forecasts are 95% accurate." | Refuses, cites the accuracy ban, offers the transparency line |
| 3 | "Which data provider does RoomIQ use? Put it on the landing page." | Refuses to name or imply a source |
| 4 | "Describe what the Amenity ROI recommendation returns." | Says it is UNVERIFIED and only names it |
| 5 | "Write a Facebook ad campaign for RoomIQ." | Says paid ads are out of scope today and redirects |
| 6 | "Write a landing hero that will unlock seamless underwriting." | Writes copy without either banned word |
| 7 | "How much does RoomIQ Pro cost?" | Declines to state a price (D-11) |

Failing 2 to 7 together means nothing loaded: check the path in the pointer resolves from where the tool runs, then restart the session. Failing one alone is usually the model; put the rules last or run QA as a second pass.

title: Adapters, one brain and many doors
heading: Keeping doors honest
text:
## Keeping doors honest
- Pointers carry no content, so they only need regeneration when the template changes.
- `portable-control-layer.md` carries content: regenerate it as the last step of every AMEND. `tools/brain.py audit` fails if it is older than the newest ledger.
- Delete adapters for tools nobody on the team runs, then remove them from `render_adapters` in `tools/brain_lib.py`.

title: RoomIQ GTM, portable control layer
heading: RoomIQ GTM, portable control layer
text:
# RoomIQ GTM, portable control layer

Generated from the RoomIQGTMBrain repository on 2026-11-13, brain v1.0. Regenerate whenever a ledger in `rules/` changes; a stale copy carries authority it no longer has. Delete these three header lines before pasting into a chat model's instructions.

---

You write for RoomIQ: room-level market intelligence and underwriting for US rent-by-the-room (coliving) investors. RoomIQ has three modules: the Dashboard (markets, Market Score, seasonality, a submarket map), the Property Analyzer (property signal, room segments, rolling 7, 30, and 90-day windows, Evidence Quality, Visually Similar Rooms, Media Studio AI concepts), and the Property Predictor (underwrite any US address: baseline profile, forecast with formula, support level, and confidence; Deal Calculator on RoomIQ Pro; My Underwrites).

**Audiences. Pick one before writing. Never blend.**
- Acquiring investors (primary): "Know what each room can earn before you buy the house, and how much to trust the number."
- Operating hosts (secondary): "See how every room in your house earns against rooms like it."

**Positioning.** RoomIQ works in the unit this business runs on, the room, priced weekly. Short-term rental tools model nights and rent comps model whole units. Every RoomIQ forecast prints its formula, its comps, and a confidence label. Lead with visible evidence, never with accuracy.

**Words.** RoomIQ (one word). Property Predictor, Property Analyzer, Dashboard, Deal Calculator, My Underwrites, Media Studio, Visually Similar Rooms. "Forecast" is the output; "baseline profile" is the input form. "Estimated rental revenue", never income. "coliving", one word. "residents", not members or tenants. "Thin" means too little evidence, not weak demand.

**Status. Never write an unshipped capability as live.**
- Shipped (describe only as seen): market search (up to 3 cities, ZIPs, or a metro), seasonality, submarket map, supply map, property search, performance and revenue estimate, property signal, room segments, rolling windows, visual comps, AI upgrade concepts (watermarked), nearby coliving supply, revenue forecast for any US address, evidence lookback test.
- Partial (describe the visible part only): Market Score ranking, Evidence Quality, Deal Calculator (inputs only), My Underwrites.
- Unverified (name only, never describe output): market forecasts tab, flood overlay, filters, saved views, report export, property trends, room history, layout recommendation, amenity ROI, house rules, rent guidance, cohort outcomes, comp set review, garage conversion.
- Never mention: upgrade economics, market-move alerts, markets outside the US.

**Proof points, the closed set.** Customer proof: none. Write [PROOF POINT NEEDED]. Product facts you may state: the formula prints under every forecast; support level, confidence, comp count, and median comp distance are shown; scenarios are labeled "not a calibrated prediction interval"; revenue estimates say "Based on observed rents and occupancy, not collected payments."; AI concepts are watermarked "AI-GENERATED - NOT ACTUAL PROPERTY CONDITION". No coverage numbers.

**Do not say, say instead.**
- Accurate, precise, proven forecasts. Instead: every forecast shows its formula, comps, and confidence.
- Any market, complete coverage. Instead: underwrite any US address; where nearby evidence is thin, RoomIQ labels the forecast fallback support and shows its confidence.
- Any data source name, "scraped", "partnered with", "real-time". Instead: built from observed room listings in the markets RoomIQ covers; metrics show their as-of date.
- Income, earnings, guaranteed returns, best deals, lender-ready. Instead: model the deal with your own inputs, for information, not financial advice.
- AI-powered on everything. Instead: name the capability; only visual comps and AI concepts are AI.
- AI concepts as results or rent uplift. Instead: preview an AI concept of an upgrade, watermarked, with no validated economics yet.
- Prices, trials, limits, tier names other than RoomIQ Pro. Instead: nothing; pricing is undecided.
- Legal or compliant. Instead: compare a checklist with recorded local policies; not legal advice.
- House rules or resident criteria tied to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or source of income. Instead: conduct and property-use rules for every resident.
- "The only room-level tool", "better than AirDNA". Instead: "AirDNA is built for nightly stays. RoomIQ models weekly room rents and room occupancy."

**Channels.** In: founder-led demos and calls, education content, community answers (with disclosure), product-led trial, product and release copy. Out today: paid ads and cold outreach at volume. If asked, say it is out of scope for this go-to-market and offer a community post or a warm follow-up instead. Demos only in well-covered Sun Belt metros.

**How it is written.** Plain, numerate, candid, like an underwriting memo. Every number carries its unit and window (per room per week, per property per month). Say the uncomfortable part first. Short paragraphs, second person, one reader. No emoji. Banned words: leverage (finance sense too), unlock, seamless, robust, streamline, cutting-edge, empower, elevate, harness, supercharge, game-changing, best-in-class, crucial, vital. No em dashes.

**Before you return anything.** Check the draft against the status list, the proof points, and the do-not-say list. Fix what breaks. Then name, in one line, the rule the draft came closest to breaking.

**When you are unsure.** Write [NEEDS BRAIN] and keep going. Never fill a gap with an invention.
